Fact.Name: Taxable dependent care benefits allocated to the primary filer, Form 2441 line 26
Fact.Description:
THE TAXPAYER'S OWN SPLIT of the Form 2441 line-26 taxable residue between two spouses on a joint return. The primary filer's share is attested here and the secondary filer's is the REMAINDER (/cdccTaxableBenefitsAllocatedToSecondaryFiler), which is the one-amount intake shape: a single number cannot express a pair that fails to sum to the residue, so the arithmetic half of coherence is unrepresentable rather than merely refused.
AN ATTESTATION, NEVER A DERIVATION, AND THIS MODULE HAS ALREADY PAID FOR GETTING THAT WRONG ONCE. The 2026-08-04 fill of /cdccDeemedMonthsAllocatedToOneSpouse recorded that its own contract's claim - that assigning every overlapped month to the lower earner maximises the credit - was FALSE: two worked returns on the same statute put the maximiser at opposite ends of the range. The benefits split is the same shape one line up the form. Neither section 129 nor section 21 nor Publication 503 prints an allocation rule for the line-26 residue, and Form 2441 Part III carries ONE line 18/19 earned-income pair and ONE line-21 limit for the whole return, so there is no printed per-spouse split to read off. The ABSENCE of a rule is the finding, and it is why the choice is the filer's.
WHY A SPLIT CHANGES ANYTHING. Section 21(d)(1)(B) caps the expenses taken into account at the LESSER of the two spouses' earned incomes, and the taxable residue is added to the receiving spouse's earned income for Form 2441 lines 4 and 5. Moving a dollar of residue from the higher earner to the lower one therefore raises the smaller of the two, which is the term that binds. That is the whole mechanism, and it is why an INTERIOR split can beat both whole-to-one-spouse assignments, which is exactly the population /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution refuses.
UNANSWERED IS SAFE AND STAYS REFUSED. There is no complete-safe DEFAULT dollar here: any number this dictionary invented would be a derivation, and a $0 default would silently assign the whole residue to the secondary filer. So the writable carries no default, and while it is unanswered /cdccTaxableBenefitsSplitIsAttested is false, every downstream Switch takes the arm it took before this fill, and the knockout keeps refusing. REFUSED, never DEFAULTED.

Fact.Name: The return is one where the taxpayer may allocate taxable benefits between spouses
Fact.Description:
THE POPULATION THE SPLIT INTAKE IS OFFERED TO. It is EXACTLY /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution's population, not a narrower one. The two paragraphs below explain why the carryover and forfeiture legs were once excluded, and BOTH ARE NOW SPENT: each leg's missing input is its own writable (/writableCdccCarryoverAmountAllocatedToPrimaryFiler and /writableCdccForfeitedCreditsAllocatedToPrimaryFiler), and with them the per-spouse pools sum to Form 2441 line 23 exactly, so a coherent split always exists and the check can verify the one it is given. What replaced the two Not() conjuncts is a single Any that is byte-identical to the shipping guard's own second conjunct. The answeredness of the two new attributions is NOT tested here - it belongs to /cdccBenefitsAttributionIsAttested, one level up, because it is an ANSWER and this fact is a POPULATION.
The 2026-08-22 text follows, unedited. It is deliberately NARROWER than /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution's population by exactly one conjunct: the grace-period carryover leg is excluded.
WHY THE CARRYOVER LEG IS EXCLUDED, and this is a measurement rather than a preference. Section 129(a) puts the taxable excess in the income of the employee whose employer paid the benefit, so each spouse's share is capped at that spouse's OWN reported benefits - income:/cdccPrimaryFilerMaximumEarnedIncomeAdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits and its secondary twin, both shipping. /cdccCarryoverAmountFromPriorTaxYear is a RETURN-LEVEL amount with no per-filer attribution anywhere in this tree, and it enters the residue through Form 2441 line 15. So on a carryover return the line-26 residue can EXCEED the sum of the two caps, and NO coherent split exists at all: an intake offered there would refuse every honest answer. Attributing a carryover to a spouse is a real missing input, and it is named as the owed arm of the rebody contract on /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution.
THE FORFEITURE LEG IS EXCLUDED TOO, ADDED 2026-08-22 BY REVIEW, AND ITS REASON IS NOT THE CARRYOVER'S. Form 2441 line 14 is "the amount, if any, you forfeited or carried forward to 2026", it is SUBTRACTED at line 15, and /writableCdccForfeitedCredits is return-level with no per-filer attribution. A spouse's true ceiling on a forfeiture return is their box 10 LESS their own share of the forfeiture, and this graph cannot compute that share. But unlike the carryover leg a coherent split ALWAYS EXISTS here - the residue is at most (P - Fp) + (S - Fs) - so the defect is not unsatisfiability, it is that the check CANNOT VERIFY the answer it is given: satisfiable-but-unverifiable. Measured before it was fixed, on the fixture now committed as cdcc-benefits-split-forfeiture-still-refused: box 10 2,000/1,500 with 1,000 forfeited gives a residue of 2,000 whose true split needs the primary to take at least 1,500, yet the pre-fix check admitted an attested 500 and the return computed a credit of 340.00 where the largest credit section 129 permits is 200.00.
With neither leg present the ceilings always admit a solution, which is why the three are separated here: the residue is at most the two spouses' combined box-10 benefits P + S, and min(residue, P) + min(residue, S) is at least residue whenever residue is at most P + S.
THE LAST CONJUNCT IS WHAT MAKES A SPLIT NECESSARY rather than merely possible. income:/cdccMaximumCreditRequiresUnsupportedCalculation is the negation of the two whole-to-one-spouse assignments that already ship, so it is true precisely on the INTERIOR of the range - where neither degenerate assignment produces the maximum credit. Where a degenerate assignment already wins, this fact is FALSE and the shipping arms keep computing untouched, which is what holds every already-filing return byte-identical.

Fact.Name: How much of the primary filer's line-13 grace-period carryover sat in their own sole proprietorship or partnership plan
Fact.Description:
Form 2441 line 22 asks "Is any amount on line 12 or 13 from your sole proprietorship or partnership?" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2441.pdf, page 2) and line 23 then says "Subtract line 22 from line 15" (line 113). The line-12 half of that question has had a per-filer intake since the self-employed-benefits fill (/writablePrimaryFilerSelfEmployedDependentCareBenefits); THE LINE-13 HALF HAD NONE, and /cdccSelfEmployedDependentCareBenefitsAmount's own Description names the gap in terms: "A filer whose 2024 carryover came from their own proprietorship's plan therefore gets a line 22 that is UNDER-stated by that carryover." This writable is that missing half.
WHY IT IS PER FILER AND NOT ONE RETURN-LEVEL NUMBER. The figure is needed twice and only the per-filer shape serves both: once summed onto line 22, and once SUBTRACTED from the spouse's own line-23 pool (/cdccPrimaryFilerTaxableBenefitsSharePool), because that pool is an identity over line 23 and line 22 no longer cancels against line 12 alone once a carryover is in it. A single return-level number could not say whose pool to reduce.
IT IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM /writableCdccCarryoverAmountAllocatedToPrimaryFiler, which splits line 13 BY SPOUSE. This splits a spouse's own share BY PLAN KIND — an employer's plan or their own unincorporated business's. The two must not be read as answering each other; that confusion is exactly what /cdccSelfEmployedDependentCareBenefitsAmount's Description warns against.
WHY A PROPRIETOR'S OWN PLAN CAN HOLD A GRACE-PERIOD CARRYOVER AT ALL. The line-13 instruction is written for "an employer-provided dependent care plan" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 5), and IRC 129(e)(4) makes a sole proprietor his own employer and a partnership the employer of each partner — which is also why the printed line 22 reaches line 13 and not line 12 alone. No interpretation is needed: line 22 names line 13 on its face.
UNANSWERED IS $0 AND SAFE. /cdccPrimaryFilerSelfEmployedCarryoverPortion is the complete-safe reader; nothing reads this writable directly.
SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, non-negative by declared Limit, rounded to whole dollars by the reader. A negative answer cannot reach line 22: the reader floors with GreaterOf, because a writable Limit Min is a write-time declaration and is not enforced on resolution.

Fact.Description:

THE GATE HAS AN IsComplete FIRST CONJUNCT ON PURPOSE. All(IsComplete(x), x) is Complete(false) when x is Incomplete, so this fact is COMPLETE on every return including one that has not reached the carryover question at all. Both tests are needed — a share that exceeds this spouse's attribution can still be under the return's line 13 and still leave this spouse's pool positive. Same discipline as /cdccCarryoverAmountAllocatedToSecondaryFiler, which lets a remainder go negative rather than flooring a bad attribution out of sight.

Fact.Description:

The MFJ Switch is /cdccSelfEmployedDependentCareBenefitsAmount's own, deliberately identical, for the reason that fact gives — line 22 must not put on the form more than lines 12 and 13 contain, or line 23 subtracts money that was never added.
THE LITERAL READING OF LINE 22 IS THE WHOLE OF THIS FACT. Line 22 asks about an amount "on line 12 or 13" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2441.pdf, page 2). It does not name line 14, and line 23 is "Subtract line 22 from line 15" (line 113) with line 15 being "Combine lines 12 through 14" (line 88). So the self-employed part of a line-14 forfeiture is NOT subtracted from line 22: no printed line says to, and inventing that subtraction would be arithmetic no source states. See the FILL-PRIORITY row for the refused alternative reading.
READ ONLY FROM INSIDE LINE 22'S ANSWERED ARM. This fact reads filingStatus, so a return that answers none of the four self-employed intakes never evaluates it — /cdccSelfEmployedDependentCareBenefitsAmount's outer gate is what keeps line 22 free of filing-status completeness, and this fact sits inside that gate's Then.

WHERE THERE IS A CARRYOVER it takes two things: the question is answered, and the answer leaves a non-negative remainder for the spouse. The remainder half is the only arithmetic a one-amount intake CAN get wrong - the sum is structural and the sign of the primary part is the writable's own Min-0 Limit - and it is checked here rather than in the pool below so that the two failures stay distinguishable: an over-large part is a bad ANSWER, a negative pool is a bad ATTRIBUTION PATTERN.
THE FALSE TAIL IS DEFINITIVE. Every case is total, so this fact is Complete wherever /hasReportedCarryOverAmountFromPriorTaxYear is, which is what lets the knockout take it through /cdccTaxableBenefitsSplitIsAttested without becoming Incomplete.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's own part of the Form 2441 line-23 pool the residue is drawn from
Fact.Description:
THE PER-SPOUSE DECOMPOSITION OF FORM 2441 LINE 23, and it is an identity rather than an estimate. Line 15 is "Combine lines 12 through 14" and line 23 is "Subtract line 22 from line 15", so line 23 is (line 12 + line 13 - line 14) - line 22. Line 12 is the two spouses' box 10 totals PLUS the sole-proprietorship amount, and line 22 is that same sole-proprietorship amount, so it cancels and line 23 is exactly (box10 + carryover - forfeiture) for the primary filer PLUS the same three terms for the secondary. This fact is the first of those two sums.
WHY THAT IDENTITY IS THE WHOLE OF THIS UNIT. The residue is line 23 less line 25, so the residue never exceeds the two pools combined. Where both pools are at least $0 that makes min(residue, poolP) + min(residue, poolS) at least the residue, so a coherent split ALWAYS EXISTS - which is precisely what a grace-period carryover took away while it had no per-filer attribution, and what a forfeiture made unverifiable rather than impossible.
BOX 10 AND NOT THE LINE-12 TOTAL, inherited unchanged from /cdccPrimaryFilerTaxableBenefitsShareCeiling's own reading: the sole-proprietorship benefit is stripped at line 22 before the residue exists, so it is not in the pool being divided.
IT CAN GO BELOW $0, AND THAT IS NOT A BUG IN THIS FACT. A forfeiture attributed to a spouse beyond their box 10 plus their attributed carryover leaves this negative; /cdccBenefitsAttributionIsAttested tests for exactly that and refuses the return rather than letting a negative ceiling silently reject every answer. Flooring it at $0 here would hide the condition and break the identity above.

The 2025 Instructions for Form 2441 put line 14 inside line 12 ("enter on line 14 the total of the following amounts included on line 12"), so a forfeiture is drawn from the line-12 pool - but line 12 carries the sole-proprietorship amount that line 22 strips out again, so a spouse who has BOTH a sole-proprietorship benefit and a forfeiture larger than their box 10 has a line-14 / line-22 overlap that no printed line resolves. Fact.Description:
The second operand of the LesserOf is /cdccPrimaryFilerTaxableBenefitsSharePool, which is box 10 PLUS this spouse's attributed share of the Form 2441 line-13 carryover LESS their attributed share of the line-14 forfeiture. THE PARAGRAPHS BELOW APPLY TO THE POOL - the sole-proprietorship benefit is excluded, for the line-22 reason they give - and the pool fact inherits that reading. A carryover and a forfeiture do not have to be excluded from the population to keep the ceilings honest, because they are attributed. On a return with neither, the pool is the box-10 CollectionSum and this fact equals it to the cent.
THE POOL THAT ACTUALLY FORMS THE RESIDUE, WHICH IS BOX 10 AND NOTHING ELSE, and this fact exists because the obvious ceiling is the wrong one. Form 2441 line 23 is "Subtract line 22 from line 15", and line 22 is the part of the benefits that came from the filer's own sole proprietorship or partnership - so the self-employed benefit is STRIPPED before line 26 is reached and is not in the residue being split at all. income:/cdccPrimaryFilerMaximumEarnedIncomeAdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits, the shipping ceiling this fact replaces FOR THE SPLIT ONLY, is a LesserOf against /cdccPrimaryFilerDependentCareBenefitsAmount, which is box 10 PLUS the sole-proprietorship benefit. Using it as the coherence ceiling imports a pool the residue does not contain and lets a spouse be handed more of the residue than their employer ever reported.
THE SHIPPING FACT HAS OTHER READERS - the two whole-to-one-spouse assignment flags and the pre-fill fallback allocation - which is the reason to keep this ceiling separate. This fact is narrower and is read only by /cdccTaxableBenefitsSplitIsCoherent. The second LesserOf operand of income:/cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerMaximumEarnedIncomeAdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits is /cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerEarnedIncomeAdjustmentPool, which is the Form 2441 line-12 amount PLUS the spouse's attributed line-13 carryover where the attribution is attested and IS that same line-12 amount everywhere else. This fact is still box 10 with the line-22 sole-proprietorship amount stripped, which the ceiling over there deliberately is not.
WHY IT IS STILL A LesserOf AGAINST THE RESIDUE: a spouse cannot take more of the residue than the residue is, and keeping that term is what makes the coherence set always satisfiable once the carryover and forfeiture legs are excluded - the residue is at most the two box-10 totals combined, so min(residue, P) + min(residue, S) is at least the residue.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's own dependent care money for the Form 2441 line-4 adjustment: line 12 plus their attributed line 13
Fact.Description:
THE POOL THE WHOLE-TO-ONE-SPOUSE ADJUSTMENT IS CAPPED AT, and it exists because the shipping cap was one form line short. income:/cdccPrimaryFilerMaximumEarnedIncome- AdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits caps this filer's part of the taxable residue at /cdccPrimaryFilerDependentCareBenefitsAmount, which is Form 2441 LINE 12 - box 10 plus this filer's own sole-proprietorship or partnership benefit. On a joint return with a carryover the two line-12 caps can therefore sum to LESS than the residue, and the part above them reaches NEITHER spouse's Form 2441 line 4 NOR line 5: the credit is UNDER-stated, taxpayer-adverse.
MEASURED, NOT THEORISED, and the fixture that measured it is committed: tests/nodes/ty2025/form2441/cdcc-carryover-underallocation-unattributed is MFJ with box 10 of 2,000.00 for the primary filer alone and a 1,000.00 carryover; the residue is 2,500.00 and the two per-filer figures are 2,000.00 and 0.00, so 500.00 of it lands nowhere. This fact widens the OFFER of the same routed question (/writableCdccCarryoverAmountAllocatedToPrimaryFiler) to that population. No new writable and no new guard. With that split the claim holds as restated above, and the reviewer's own case is committed both ways as cdcc-carryover-underallocation-both-box10-{unattributed,attributed-files}.]
UNANSWERED IS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR TO THE CENT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, and it is deliberately a DEFAULTED rather than a REFUSED cell for this population: these returns file today, and refusing them to collect an answer would take a filed return away. Three ways in: a return with no carryover reads the second arm and this fact IS /cdccPrimaryFilerDependentCareBenefitsAmount; a carryover return that has not answered fails /cdccCarryoverAttributionIsAttested and reads the same second arm; an OVER-attributed answer (a part above line 13) fails it too, so no ceiling can ever be raised by money the return does not have. Witnessed by -unattributed and -overattributed, which assert today's figures on both sides of this fill.
THE IsComplete CONJUNCT IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS FIRST ON PURPOSE. /hasReportedCarryOverAmountFromPriorTaxYear is a Placeholder on a return that has not answered the carryover gate at all, and /cdccCarryoverAttributionIsAttested inherits that through its own Not() arm. Without the IsComplete test in front, this fact would go Placeholder on returns whose line-12 amount is Complete today, so the pool would be LESS complete than the thing it replaces. With it, this fact is Complete exactly where /cdccPrimaryFilerDependentCareBenefitsAmount is - witnessed by cdcc-carryover-underallocation-gate-unanswered.
WHAT THIS FACT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, named rather than absorbed. (a) It does NOT subtract the attributed Form 2441 line-14 forfeiture. The shipping cap has never subtracted it, this fill does not change that blindness by one cent, and subtracting it is taxpayer-ADVERSE and would move /flowShowCdccQualifyingPersonsLoop, which reads the same two income facts - a different unit's decision, and it is recorded as a named gap in cdcc_memory.json. (b) It does NOT strip a sole-proprietorship carryover at Form 2441 line 22. This cap reads the UN-stripped line-12 pool by its own long-standing construction (that is exactly why /cdccPrimaryFilerTaxableBenefitsShareCeiling exists as a separate, stripped ceiling for the split), so an un-stripped line-13 addend is consistent with it; the per-source attribution that would refine it is not built.

Fact.Name: The attested split is one section 129(a) permits
Fact.Description:
THE COHERENCE TEST, and it is the section 129(a) per-employee ceiling rather than a plausibility check. Each spouse's share of the taxable residue may not exceed the benefits that spouse's OWN employer reported - Form W-2 box 10 plus that spouse's own sole proprietorship or partnership benefit - because section 129(a)(1) excludes from the gross income OF AN EMPLOYEE what THAT employee's employer paid, and 129(a)(2)(B) puts the excess over the ceiling in that same employee's income. The two ceilings already ship as income:/cdccPrimaryFilerMaximumEarnedIncomeAdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits and its secondary twin, each a LesserOf of the whole residue and that filer's reported benefits; this fact reuses them rather than restating the rule a third time. [DATED NOTE 2026-08-24, unit cdcc-carryover-underallocation: "that filer's reported benefits" in the sentence above is, as of that date, that filer's Form 2441 line-12 amount PLUS their attributed line-13 carryover where the attribution is attested (/cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerEarnedIncomeAdjustmentPool). The sentence's other claim - that this fact REUSES those two - was already false before this note: the paragraph immediately below records the 2026-08-22 correction that moved this fact onto /cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerTaxableBenefitsShareCeiling. Both readings are left standing because the paragraph below is the record of why they diverged.]
THE POOL IS BOX 10 AND NOT THE FORM 2441 LINE 12 TOTAL, CORRECTED 2026-08-22 BY REVIEW. The first cut of this fact read the shipping income:/cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerMaximumEarnedIncomeAdjustmentFromTaxableBenefits, whose LesserOf is against box 10 PLUS the spouse's own sole-proprietorship benefit. That is the line-12 pool, and line 12 is NOT what line 26 is computed on: line 23 is "Subtract line 22 from line 15" and line 22 is exactly the sole-proprietorship amount, so the self-employed benefit is stripped before the residue exists. Reading it as a ceiling let a spouse be handed residue their EMPLOYER never reported. Measured before it was fixed, on the fixture now committed as cdcc-benefits-split-soleprop-ceiling-refused: box 10 2,000/500 with a 1,000 sole-proprietorship benefit gives a residue of 2,500 whose only coherent split is 2,000/500, yet the pre-fix check admitted an attested 1,000 and the return computed a credit of 400.00 where the correct figure is 200.00. The ceilings this fact now reads, /cdcc{Primary,Secondary}FilerTaxableBenefitsShareCeiling, are box 10 alone. [AMENDED 2026-08-24, unit cdcc-benefits-distribution: "box 10 alone" became "box 10 plus that spouse's attributed line-13 carryover less their attributed line-14 forfeiture" when those two attributions landed. The sole-proprietorship correction recorded above is UNTOUCHED by that - line 22 still strips it - and on a return with neither a carryover nor a forfeiture the two ceilings are unchanged to the cent. The answeredness of the two attributions is checked by /cdccBenefitsAttributionIsAttested rather than here, so this fact still tests exactly one thing.]
THE SUM AND SIGN HALVES OF COHERENCE ARE NOT TESTED HERE BECAUSE THEY CANNOT FAIL. The sum is structural (the secondary share is the remainder, not a second answer) and the primary share is floored at $0 by the writable's own Limit. What is left is the only half that CAN fail, and it is the half a one-amount intake cannot make impossible.
NEGATIVITY OF THE REMAINDER IS COVERED TOO, without a third conjunct: the primary ceiling is a LesserOf against the residue itself, so a share that passes the first test is at most the residue and the remainder is at least $0.
WHY THE VIOLATION IS ROUTED THROUGH THE KNOCKOUT AND NOT A NEW BLOCK. A dynamic upper bound is not expressible as a Writable Limit in this dictionary - every one of the Limit elements in dictionary/ty2025/ holds a literal, none holds a Dependency, measured rather than assumed - so the ceiling has to be a derived test. Routing it into the SHIPPING guard, by withholding attestation, keeps the refusal in the one place that already refuses this population and adds no new refusal surface: an incoherent answer leaves the return exactly where an unanswered one leaves it, which is refused and told.

Fact.Name: The taxpayer has given a usable split of the taxable benefits
Fact.Description:
THE ONE GATE every consumer of the split reads: the return is one where a split is offered, the taxpayer answered, and the answer is one section 129(a) permits. It is false in all three failure directions - unavailable, unanswered, incoherent - and each of the three leaves the shipping computation exactly as it stood before this fill and leaves /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution refusing. A FOURTH failure direction is UNATTRIBUTED - a return whose Form 2441 line-13 carryover or line-14 forfeiture has not been assigned to a spouse, or has been assigned so that one spouse's section 129(a) pool falls below $0. It is carried by the added conjunct /cdccBenefitsAttributionIsAttested and it collapses into the same place as the other three, on purpose and for the same reason. On a return with neither amount that conjunct is TRUE by construction, so nothing the predecessor freed moves. The IsComplete discipline below holds for all four directions, because the added conjunct is a Switch with definitive tails over Complete Dollars.
THAT COLLAPSE IS THE POINT. A filer who answers incoherently is in the same position as one who has not answered: told, and not filed. The alternative - computing on a bad answer, or adding a second refusal surface beside the one that already covers this population - would either file a wrong number or split one refusal into two that must then be kept in step.
THE THREE-WAY IsComplete DISCIPLINE. Every conjunct is itself total: availability is an All over shipping booleans, and coherence is a Switch with a False tail. So this fact is Complete on every return, which is what lets /flowKnockoutBenefitsDistribution take it as a plain conjunct without becoming Incomplete anywhere.
